question: A restaurant's menu lists the dishes you can order. Why can the kitchen replace its stoves without telling any customer?
options: Customers depend only on what the menu promises, not on how the kitchen works
Customers only notice the price, so anything else may change
The menu is printed from the kitchen's equipment list, so it updates itself
The kitchen prints a new menu every time it changes
explanation: The menu is the contract, like an API. As long as the dishes on it stay the same, everything behind it can change. Customers do notice when a dish is removed or changed, not only the price, which is why breaking changes to an API need a new version. The menu describes what you can order, not the equipment.
